name: Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Power Station (Kapar)
status_detail: Operational · GF1 commissioned 1985-1986, GF3 taken over in 2000
summary: Malaysia's largest power station, on the coast at Kapar near Klang. Operated by Kapar Energy Ventures, a joint venture of TNB and Malakoff, it burns coal and gas across four generating facilities and anchors the Klang Valley's electricity supply.

scale.label: Fuels
scale.value: Coal and natural gas, with oil firing capability

why_it_matters: The biggest single generator on the Klang Valley grid and a defining landmark of the Klang coast. Its coal-fired units sit at the centre of Malaysia's energy-transition debate just as data centre demand pushes power consumption up.
questions_to_follow: What is the retirement or repowering timeline for the older coal-fired GF1-GF3 units?
How does the plant's output mix shift as Selangor's data centre load grows?
location_precision: Kapar Energy Ventures station, Kapar. Coordinates are the plant site as published on the station's Wikipedia page.

sources.title: Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Power Station

history.event: First GF1 units commissioned; GF2 followed in 1988-1989 and GF4 gas turbines later completed the four-phase layout.
Station officially opened by the Sultan of Selangor and named after Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah.
GF3 (2 x 500 MW) taken over, keeping it the largest power station in Malaysia.
